question:
A 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and ulcerative colitis presents with a
3-week history of left lower quadrant pain and frequent bloody diarrhea. He was started on prednisone
40 mg twice daily five weeks ago for a colitis flare, which initially improved but has since worsened over

the past three weeks, accompanied by low-grade fevers. He denies nausea, vomiting, or other new
symptoms. His ulcerative colitis, diagnosed by biopsy two years ago, was previously limited to the
rectum and sigmoid colon and well controlled on azathioprine until the current flare. A colonoscopy six
months ago showed inactive colitis confined to the rectum. On examination, his temperature is 38.2°C,
and his heart rate is 92 beats per minute. His abdomen is diffusely tender to palpation without rebound
or guarding. Laboratory studies reveal a leukocyte count of 8600/mm³ (reference range, 4500–11,000),
and his metabolic panel is within normal limits. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals pancolitis.
Stool tests for Clostridioides difficile and bacterial cultures are negative. What is the most appropriate
next step in management for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Perform a CT-guided biopsy of the
colon (B) Order stool culture and serum PCR testing for cytomegalovirus (C) Initiate infliximab therapy
immediately (D) Start empiric intravenous glucocorticoids without additional evaluation (E) Increase the
dose of azathioprine (F) Start oral mesalamine therapy (G) Start metronidazole and ceftriaxone (H)
Order a full colonoscopy with biopsy (I) Administer intravenous fluids and monitor symptoms (J)
Perform sigmoidoscopy with biopsy
 A. Order stool culture and serum PCR testing for cytomegalovirus
B. Perform a CT-guided biopsy of the colon
C. Order a full colonoscopy with biopsy
D. Start oral mesalamine therapy
E. Start empiric intravenous glucocorticoids without additional evaluation
F. Increase the dose of azathioprine
G. Start metronidazole and ceftriaxone
H. Perform sigmoidoscopy with biopsy
I. Initiate infliximab therapy immediately
J. Administer intravenous fluids and monitor symptoms
